text:
Recent evidence does not establish a universal sampled-softmax advantage. [Di Teodoro et al. (2024/2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07770) show that single-negative categorical cross-entropy equals BPR; their analysis gives BCE the strongest worst-case probabilistic ranking bound under negative sampling. [Scaled cross-entropy (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14238) instead reports benefits from increasing the sampled normalizing term. These results support controlling negative count and loss normalization before attributing improvements to the objective. [RecSys 2025 work on logQ correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) also distinguishes deterministically included positives from sampled negatives; correction choices affect gradient weighting.

Proposed diagnostic, rather than a published validated protocol: compare BCE-1, BCE-32 and softmax-32 at identical checkpoints using fixed training prefixes and a shared pool of 32 unique eligible negatives; BCE-1 uses a predetermined member. Before updates, ranks must match across objectives. Measure paired rank changes after bounded, matched updates, alongside raw logits, margins and embedding norms. Define negative-gradient concentration as the top-1/top-5 share of summed absolute negative-logit derivatives. Report gradient norms and per-parameter RMS separately for item embeddings and encoder parameters; tied embeddings require distinguishing input-path and scoring-path contributions. State BCE positive/negative weighting explicitly so changing negative count does not silently change loss scale.

Stratify by training-only popularity: [2024 sequential-recommendation experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) found random negative sampling favored head items. Keep full-catalog ranks and unseen-item recommendations auxiliary: [sampled-metric analysis](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651) shows sampled evaluation can disagree with full-catalog model ordering. Preserve the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, 200 users/category and 99 negatives as the selection criterion.
